title: 休日の業務連絡「拒否」が6割超　企業も配慮の「つながらない権利」が法制化に至らぬ事情
extracted_text: 休日はリフレッシュしたいと思う人が少なくない中、勤務時間外の業務連絡に対応しない「つながらない権利」が国でも議論され、注目を集めている。テレワークの普及などで仕事と私生活の区別が曖昧になり、ワークライフバランスに配慮すべきだとの問題意識が背景にある。各社は働き方改革の重要性を認識しつつ、職種によって連絡せざるを得ないケースもあり、明確にルール化している企業は少数派のようだ。 国内では昨年、厚生労働相の諮問機関、労働政策審議会の分科会で、働き方改革の一環として議題に上がった。労働者側は法制化を求める一方、経営者側は「業務遂行の方法に関わる面が強く、法律で義務化すべきではない」などと主張して意見の一致に至らず、法改正は見送られた経緯がある。 関西に拠点を置く企業では、関西みらい銀行が運用ルールを整備している。「勤務時間外の対応・判断・返信を伴う業務は原則として行わない」といい、管理職に対しても、勤務時間外の対応を前提とした連絡や指示を行わないよう周知。組織全体で適切な働き方を実現する仕組みとしているという。
translated_text: With many people wanting to refresh during holidays, the 'right to disconnect' from work-related communications outside working hours is being discussed at the national level and is drawing attention. Against this backdrop, awareness has grown that tele-work adoption has blurred the distinctions between work and personal life, making it necessary to consider work-life balance. While each company recognizes the importance of work style reform, there are cases depending on the job position where contact is unavoidable, and it appears that only a minority of companies have clearly established rules. In Japan last year, the issue was raised at a subcommittee of the Labor Policy Council, an advisory body to the Minister of Health, Labor and Welfare, as part of work style reform. While workers advocated for legalization, business leaders argued that 'it strongly relates to how work is performed and should not be mandated by law,' and the parties failed to reach agreement, resulting in the legislative reform being postponed. Among companies based in the Kansai region, Kansai Mirai Bank has established operational rules. They state that 'work involving responses, judgments, or replies outside working hours will in principle not be conducted,' and they have informed management to avoid making contacts or giving instructions assuming responses outside working hours. The bank says this implements a system across the organization to achieve proper working styles.
title_en: Over 60% Refuse Work Contacts on Holidays; Why Companies Haven't Legalized the 'Right to Disconnect' Despite Growing Need for Consideration
